# What you should know
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/v2/docs/what_to_know



The PawaPay Merchant API simplifies integrating mobile money into your payment flows.
It provides a single standardised API to connect to Mobile Money Operators (MMOs) providing mobile money services across Africa.

The following chapters introduce some important aspects of mobile money and working with financial APIs to help you build a high-quality integration that your customers will love and that is easy to operate.

## Callbacks

The PawaPay Merchant API is **asynchronous**. This is necessary to provide high performance and quality payment infrastructure that is able to process millions of payments every day.

When you call any financial endpoint ([payout](/v2/api-reference/payouts/initiate-payout), [deposit](/v2/api-reference/deposits/initiate-deposit), [refund](/v2/api-reference/refunds/initiate-refund)), the response will confirm whether the transaction is **accepted** or **rejected** for processing.
A transaction may be rejected due to reasons such as using the same ID more than once or the provider being unavailable at the moment.

If the response confirms that the payment has been **accepted** for processing, it will take some time for it to process (remember that for deposits, the user needs to enter their PIN on their phone).
There are two ways to **determine the final status** of a payment.

### Polling for status

First, you can use the corresponding `Check Status` endpoint for the transaction type to periodically **check the status of a payment**.

### Through callbacks

Second, you can configure callback URLs in the PawaPay Dashboard.
This will automatically **send a callback to your configured callback URL** as soon as a payment has reached its final status.
You will have to implement a callback handler that is able to receive calls from our platform and handle them accordingly.

![Deposit with PawaPay Merchant API](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/KEPFVQN1WP0Rqmg8/images/deposit_flow.jpg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=KEPFVQN1WP0Rqmg8\&q=85\&s=73f8106fb17c083dbf7cfd9672a78f60)

### Setting up callbacks

Callback URLs are configured from the PawaPay Dashboard.
You can find instructions on how to do that from the [PawaPay Dashboard Docs](/dashboard/other/system_conf/callback_urls).

### Handling callbacks

When implementing your callback handler, please consider the following points.

* Your endpoint for receiving callbacks must be **idempotent**.
  * Sending a callback more than once for the same payment should not cause a double credit or debit in your system.
* Your endpoint needs to allow us to `POST` the callback.
* Make sure you use an SSL certificate from a **trusted CA**.
* We will make up to **8 delivery attempts** over approximately **25 minutes**. See [Callback delivery attempts](#callback-delivery-attempts) below.
* We expect you to return `HTTP 200 OK` response to consider the callback **delivered**.
* If the callback delivery fails, you can trigger a resend of the callback within **90 days** of the payment being initiated. This can be done by:
  * Calling the respective `Resend callback` endpoint
  * Manually from the [PawaPay Dashboard](/dashboard/transactions/callback_resend).
  * For payments older than 90 days, callbacks can no longer be resent. The status of the payment remains available through the `Check Status` endpoints.
* The endpoint should be **accessible to our platform**.
  * Ensure that you have excluded the callback endpoint from your application's regular authentication system.
  * If you are using IP whitelisting, whitelist the below IPs to ensure we can deliver callbacks to you.

### Callback delivery attempts

When a payment reaches its final status, we send the callback straight away.
If your endpoint does not return `HTTP 200 OK`, we try again on the following schedule.

| Attempt | Sent at | Wait before next attempt |
| - | - | - |
| 1 | 0:00 | 1 minute |
| 2 | 1:00 | 1 minute |
| 3 | 2:00 | 3 minutes |
| 4 | 5:00 | 5 minutes |
| 5 | 10:00 | 5 minutes |
| 6 | 15:00 | 5 minutes |
| 7 | 20:00 | 5 minutes |
| 8 | 25:00 | — |

* Times are measured from when the callback is first sent. They are approximate.
* Once your endpoint returns `HTTP 200 OK`, the callback is **delivered** and no further attempts are made.
* If attempt 8 (around **25 minutes**) also fails, we stop retrying. You can then:
  * Resend the callback: [deposits](/v2/api-reference/deposits/resend-deposit-callback), [payouts](/v2/api-reference/payouts/resend-payout-callback), [refunds](/v2/api-reference/refunds/resend-refund-callback), [remittances](/v2/api-reference/remittances/resend-remittance-callback).
  * Get the final status: [deposits](/v2/api-reference/deposits/check-deposit-status), [payouts](/v2/api-reference/payouts/check-payout-status), [refunds](/v2/api-reference/refunds/check-refund-status), [remittances](/v2/api-reference/remittances/check-remittance-status).
* Because of retries, your endpoint may receive the same callback more than once. This is why it must be **idempotent**.

### Timeouts and slow responses

* We wait up to **10 seconds** to establish a connection to your callback URL and up to **30 seconds** for a response.
  If either is exceeded, the attempt counts as failed.
* Respond with `HTTP 200 OK` as soon as you have received the callback and process it asynchronously. Do not hold the connection open while you run your own business logic.
* If we detect slow responses or `HTTP 429 Too Many Requests` from your callback URL, we may skip some callback delivery attempts to avoid adding to the load on your system.

### IPs to whitelist

Callbacks from PawaPay will be coming from one of the IPs listed below.

| Environment | IP |
| - | - |
| Sandbox | 3.64.89.224/32 |
| Production | 18.192.208.15/32 |
| Production | 18.195.113.136/32 |
| Production | 3.72.212.107/32 |
| Production | 54.73.125.42/32 |
| Production | 54.155.38.214/32 |
| Production | 54.73.130.113/32 |

## MMO stability

As described in the [What's mobile money](/v2/docs/whats_mobile_money#what-does-a-payment-look-like) section, mobile money transaction chains are complex.
This means that the stability of payment services needs to be taken into account when implementing a high-quality payment flow.
PawaPay provides multiple solutions to make this easy to manage.

Our 24/7 payment operations team monitors all MMOs on our platform for instability and downtime. We stop accepting payments to those MMOs if the success rate is too low.
This information is accessible from our [provider availability](/v2/api-reference/toolkit/availability) endpoint.

You can verify before initiating the payment if the MMO is currently experiencing any problems and inform the user before they attempt the payment.
Knowing that your mobile money provider is currently unavailable is a better customer experience than having your payment fail.

Failed payments usually take longer to process, leaving the customer waiting for the final result.

To provide the best support for your customers, information about MMO availability is also published in the [PawaPay Dashboard](/dashboard/status) and [Status page](https://status.pawapay.io).
You can subscribe to updates via email, Slack and other channels to ensure your support team is always informed about any potential problems with the MMOs.

When an MMO is experiencing difficulties in successfully processing disbursements, our platform will enqueue them to be processed once the MMO is operational.
Read more about [enqueued payouts](/v2/docs/payouts#handling-enqueued-payouts-and-provider-availability).

Occasionally, MMOs experience degraded system performance, which can prevent their APIs from returning the final status of payments.
During these periods, our platform continues to accept and process payments.
We reconcile these transactions through alternative methods using our reconciliation engine.
This ensures that, when using PawaPay, all payments are eventually reconciled to their final status.
Please note that this process may take slightly longer than during normal operations.

## Transaction limits

Mobile money wallets have different limits for transactions. Most common and relevant are:

* Maximum amount of deposits/payouts in a day/week/month.
* Maximum number of deposits/payouts in a day/week/month.
* Maximum balance of a mobile money wallet.

All MMOs that you transact with through PawaPay have transaction limits.
These are the lowest and highest amounts that can be collected, disbursed or refunded with the specific MMO.
They are based on the limits of the most common wallet types of this MMO.
As the effective limits depend on the specific user's transaction history, transactions may still fail due to hitting limits.

> For example, an MMO has a 1,000 GHS maximum deposit amount.
> In reality the wallet has a limitation of 1,000 GHS total transaction value per day/week/month.
> If the user has already transacted 500 GHS during this period, a transaction of 700 GHS might still fail even though it is **accepted** by PawaPay.

You can easily find the transaction limits from our [active configuration](/v2/api-reference/toolkit/active-configuration) endpoint.

## Backwards compatibility

The PawaPay Merchant API is always backwards compatible, but should not be strictly verified against the schema as backwards compatible changes might be introduced.


# What's mobile money?
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/v2/docs/whats_mobile_money



## What is mobile money?

Mobile money is a form of digital money, where instead of a bank account and a card, people get a mobile money wallet connected to their phone number.

When people sign up for a mobile money account with their Mobile Money Operator (MMO), they undergo a 'Know Your Customer' (KYC) process, similar to opening a bank account.

Instead of ATMs and bank branches, you can put money on your mobile money wallet through an extensive agent network. Instead of getting a bank account number/IBAN, your mobile money wallet is identified by your phone number.

Mobile money enables users to send and receive funds from other mobile money users, pay bills, shop online, and receive their salaries.

Mobile money wallets have transaction limits like many modern bank accounts and cards. Most important limits are:

* Number of payments done within a day, week, or month.
* Value of payments done within a day, week, or month.
* Maximum balance of a mobile money wallet.

Users can have those limits raised by going through extended KYC processes with the MMOs.

## What does a payment look like?

Mobile money payments are different from classic card payments. They are more similar to A2A or 3-D Secure enabled card payments. Specifically, the user has to explicitly authorise each payment.

With most providers, when a user attempts to pay from their mobile money wallet, they need to enter their mobile money PIN code to authorise the payment.
The PIN code is only known by the issuer (MMO) and the owner of the mobile money wallet.
Authorisation happens between those two parties and the merchant is not involved.

![](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/E3EZK2fRT-Pq5yeq/images/pin_prompt.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=E3EZK2fRT-Pq5yeq\&q=85\&s=a7923559f4c0f3bc773ef1317582f145)

There are also some alternative authorisation methods.
Some providers require redirecting the customer to the provider's page or app to authorise the payment.

![](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/E3EZK2fRT-Pq5yeq/images/redirect_authorise.jpeg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=E3EZK2fRT-Pq5yeq\&q=85\&s=4361f9fa8d78a11f338c29a892e456b3)

Even fewer require the payment to be preauthorised.
In this case the customer needs to generate an OTP with the provider and share it with you. You then need to pass it to PawaPay to initiate the payment.

![](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/E3EZK2fRT-Pq5yeq/images/preauth_otp.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=E3EZK2fRT-Pq5yeq\&q=85\&s=0dea4de93c73154751882dfbe12ac35f)

The owner of the mobile money wallet always receives an SMS receipt whenever their balance changes.

![](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/HJiOScAQ34lKT2Kj/images/auth_sms_rwa.jpg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=HJiOScAQ34lKT2Kj\&q=85\&s=e5d5f7af3c81b946bc29cfefb496ca00)

This makes mobile money payments much more secure than classic card payments reducing fraud and chargeback risk to a minimum.

This has two important implications.

First, this expands the technical infrastructure involved in processing every single payment.
Since the user needs to enter their mobile money PIN code to authorise each payment, both the server infrastructure and the cell network infrastructure are involved in the payment chain.
The PIN code is usually requested from the user by sending a USSD message over the cell network and utilising the handset's SIM toolkit to handle user interaction.
This gives mobile money incredible accessibility as it works securely on everything from the simplest of push-button handsets all the way to flagship smartphones.
On the flip side, there's a lot involved from server infrastructure, internet connectivity, cell networks, USSD gateways, etc.

Second, the user is now part of the processing chain of each transaction.
A user attempting to initiate a payment on your website or app needs to take out their handset and enter their PIN in a limited amount of time.
Or they might not find their phone, accidentally close the PIN prompt, forget their PIN code, get a phone call, etc.

To conclude, mobile money is highly accessible and secure.
The challenges to ensure high success rates and a great customer experience are different from other payment methods.
With the PawaPay Merchant API, you have the means to make sure the customer has the best experience possible.

With the PawaPay Merchant API you can easily transact with your customers in any way you need:

* **You can collect money from them**: Funds will move from the customer's mobile money wallet into your account in PawaPay. You can do that by following our guide for [Deposits](/v2/docs/deposits) or the [Payment page](/v2/docs/payment_page).
* **You can disburse money to them**: Funds will move from your account in PawaPay to the customer's mobile money wallet. You can do that by following our guide for [Payouts](/v2/docs/payouts).
* **You can refund them**: Already collected funds will move back from your account in PawaPay to the customer's mobile money wallet. You can do that following our guide for [Refunds](/v2/docs/refunds).


# History
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/finances/history



For easy reconciliation and auditability, you can always export detailed financial statements of your wallets. Every single transaction affecting your balance is recorded on the statement.

On the statement history page, you can find all your exported wallet statements.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/statement-history-table-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Only statements generated within the last 90 days are available for download.

### Glossary of data in statements

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| Time | The date and time at which this statement export was generated. Time is in the UTC time zone. |
| Requester | The user who requested this statement export. |
| Wallet | The wallet for which this statement export was generated. |
| Statement time range | The time period that is included in this statement export. |
| Status | The current status of this statement export. One of:  **Completed**: The statement export is available to download. **Generating**: The statement export is currently being generated and will be available soon. **Failed**: The statement export failed to generate. Please try again. |


# Settlements
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/finances/settlements

Choose where, how often and how much we settle from your PawaPay wallets.

PawaPay settles the funds in your wallets to your bank accounts on a schedule you choose. You set this up once on the *Settlements* page under *Finances*, and you can change it at any time.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You need the **Settlements** or **Administrator** role to set up and view settlements. See [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles).

## Before you start

Have these details ready for each bank account you want to add:

* Account holder name
* Account number or IBAN
* Bank name and SWIFT/BIC code
* Branch name, branch address and, if it has one, branch sort code
* Country and currency of the account

You can settle to two kinds of bank account:

| Account | Currency | Wallets it can take |
| :- | :- | :- |
| Cross-border | EUR, USD or GBP | Wallets from any country, except countries that only allow local settlement |
| Local | The currency of a country where PawaPay processes your payments | Wallets from the same country and currency |

## Set up your settlements

Setup has three steps, then a summary where you can change any step before you confirm.

**1. Choose where to settle**

Add a bank account, then select the wallets that settle to it under *Your wallets*. Select *Add* to save the account.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/setup-cross-border-light.svg)

You can link some or all of your wallets to a cross-border account. Link any other wallet to a local account in its own country. Once you have a cross-border account, *Country* and *Currency* only offer the countries and currencies of your unlinked wallets.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/setup-local-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can add one cross-border account. All your cross-border settlements are paid in its currency.

A local account in XOF, XAF or CDF can also take wallets in other currencies:

| Account currency | Also takes wallets in |
| :- | :- |
| XOF | XOF from other countries, XAF, CDF, USD |
| XAF | XAF from other countries, XOF, CDF, USD |
| CDF | USD |

**2. Choose how often**

Choose *Weekly*, *Bi-weekly* or *Monthly*. Settlements always start on a Monday.

| Frequency | When we settle |
| :- | :- |
| Weekly | Every Monday |
| Bi-weekly | Every second Monday |
| Monthly | Every fourth Monday |

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/setup-frequency-light.svg)

**3. Set minimum wallet balances**

A minimum wallet balance is the amount we always leave in a wallet. We never settle it. We only settle the balance above it. For example, if a wallet has a minimum wallet balance of 500,000 XOF and a balance of 1,000,000 XOF, 500,000 XOF can be settled. Each wallet can have its own minimum.

Select *I need to set minimum balances for my wallets* to enter them. If you leave it unticked, every minimum is 0 and we settle the full balance.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/setup-minimums-light.svg)

**4. Review and confirm**

Check the summary. To change a section, select its edit icon. When everything is correct, select *Confirm your preferences*. Your first settlement starts on the next Monday.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/setup-summary-light.svg)

## When we settle

Settlements start on Mondays, at the frequency you chose. When a settlement starts, we settle the part of each wallet's balance that is above its minimum wallet balance. Funds that arrive after that are included in your next settlement.

The *Settlements* tab shows the date of your upcoming settlement. How long the funds take to reach your bank depends on the country and the account.

## How much we settle

We never settle a wallet's minimum wallet balance. When a settlement starts, only the balance above it can be settled. For example, if a wallet has a minimum wallet balance of 500,000 XOF and a balance of 1,000,000 XOF, 500,000 XOF can be settled.

The total amount being settled must also reach PawaPay's minimum settlement amount:

* **Local account:** the total amount settled to the account must be worth at least 50 USD.
* **Cross-border account:** the total amount settled to the account must be worth at least 100 USD.

A local XOF, XAF or CDF account that takes more than one wallet, or a wallet in another currency, counts as a cross-border account here.

If a wallet doesn't qualify, we skip it for that settlement and its funds stay in the wallet. A wallet is skipped when:

* its balance is 0
* its balance is not above its minimum wallet balance
* the total amount being settled is below PawaPay's minimum settlement amount
* we have temporarily paused settlements in its country

## Track your settlements

The *Settlements* tab lists your previous settlements and shows the date of your upcoming one. Each settlement has one of these statuses:

| Status | What it means |
| :- | :- |
| In progress | We have taken the funds from your wallets and are sending them to your bank. |
| Completed | We have sent the funds. Cross-border settlements show the exchange rate, and you can download the proof of payment once it's attached. |
| Cancelled | We couldn't complete the settlement. All funds were returned to your wallets. |
| Skipped | None of your wallets qualified for this settlement. |

### In progress

An *In progress* settlement shows each wallet included, the amount taken from it and the bank account it goes to. Wallets that were skipped are listed too.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-in-progress-light.svg)

If you settle to more than one bank account, you see how much from each wallet goes to each account, with the bank name and country.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-accounts-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Exchange rates for cross-border settlements are shown once the settlement is complete. To see the rates we used over the past four weeks, select *Historical FX rates*.

To see why a wallet was skipped, select its *Skipped* status.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-skipped-wallet-light.svg)

Our Treasury team may leave comments on a settlement. You'll find them in the top-right corner of the settlement.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-comment-light.svg)

### Completed

A completed cross-border settlement shows the amount settled, the exchange rate and the destination bank account. Download the proof of payment (PoP) with *PoP*.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-completed-cross-border-light.svg)

A completed local settlement shows the amount settled, the destination bank account and the proof of payment.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-completed-local-light.svg)

If your bank charged a fee, it is deducted from the amount settled. If you settle to more than one bank account, the fee is shown in the *Bank fee* column.

If you settle to one bank account, the amount next to the date is the total amount settled. When your bank charged a fee, select *Amount Breakdown* under that amount to see the amount, the bank charges and the total amount settled.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-amount-breakdown-light.svg)

### Cancelled

If we cancel a settlement, the funds go back to your wallets straight away. Our Treasury team may leave a comment explaining why.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-cancelled-light.svg)

### Skipped

A settlement is *Skipped* when none of your wallets qualified. See [How much we settle](#how-much-we-settle) for the reasons.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-skipped-light.svg)

## Change your preferences

You can change your preferences at any time on the *Configuration* tab. Changes apply from the next settlement.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-config-tab-light.svg)

### Bank accounts

To update a bank account's details, or link more wallets to it, select its edit icon. You can't change the *Country* or *Currency* of an existing account, or unlink a wallet that already settles to an account.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-config-edit-account-light.svg)

### Frequency

To change how often we settle, select the edit icon next to *How often do you want to be settled?*, choose *Weekly*, *Bi-weekly* or *Monthly*, then select *Done*.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-config-frequency-light.svg)

### Minimum wallet balances

To change how much we leave in a wallet, select the edit icon next to *Minimum wallet balances*, enter the new amount for each wallet you want to change, then select *Done*. We never settle a wallet's minimum wallet balance, only the balance above it. To settle the full balance of every wallet, untick *I need to set minimum balances for my wallets*.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-config-minimums-light.svg)

### New countries

When you start processing payments in a new country, its wallet is not settled until you link it to a bank account. The *Configuration* tab shows which countries we can't settle yet. Select the link in the message to fix it.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-config-new-country-light.svg)

You can link the new wallet to your cross-border account, or add a local account for it.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/settlements/settlement-config-map-wallet-light.svg)


# Statements
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/finances/statements



You always have access to a full financial statement for each of your wallets to be able to audit and reconcile your balance on our platform.

## Search statements

To see every single transaction on your wallet, please start by choosing:

* The time period
* A wallet

![](/images/dashboard/finances/statements-search-light.svg)

Pressing "Apply filters" will display a table with the transactions on this wallet for the selected period. You can also limit the results to specific Mobile Money Operators (MMOs) or transaction types.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can choose up to a **one-year period at a time**. For some accounts the limit is one month.
>
> A maximum of 10,000 transactions are displayed.
>
> Statement data for the current day may be up to 20 minutes behind the latest transactions.

By default, results are shown starting from the oldest transaction. You can change the order by pressing on the respective column in the header of the table.

## Export statements

After selecting the wallet and time period, press the "Export Statement" button to generate a CSV file with the results.

You will be asked to confirm this action and then taken to the [History](/dashboard/finances/history) page to download the resulting CSV file.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can choose up to a **one-year period** at a time. For some accounts the limit is one month.
>
> There is no limit to the number of transactions.
>
> The export may take some time to generate. The [History](/dashboard/finances/history) page will refresh itself automatically to show the latest status.

## Data in statements

The exported CSV file includes the following columns:

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| Creation date | The date and time when this transaction was recorded on our platform. The time is in the UTC time zone. |
| MSISDN | The phone number of the mobile money wallet that was involved in the transaction. |
| Transaction ID | The ID of this transaction as specified by you through our API. You can read more about transaction IDs from [our API docs](/v1/api-reference/deposits/request-deposit). |
| Amount | The amount of the transaction. |
| MNO | The Mobile Money Operator (MMO) that fulfilled this transaction. The table on the Statements page calls this column "Provider". |
| Type | The type of this transaction. See the list of all [transaction types](/dashboard/finances/statements#transaction-types) below. |
| Balance | Your balance after this transaction. |
| Reason | The reason for this transaction, for example, "Initial top-up" for your first top-up of this wallet. |
| Metadata | Metadata in JSON format you attached to the payments for providing additional context about the payment. Only in the CSV file. |

The table on the Statements page also shows the currency and country of each transaction.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Not all columns are populated for all transactions. For example, transactions that represent a settlement of your balance do not have an MSISDN and MMO specified.

## Transaction types

You may encounter the following transaction types in your statements:

| Transaction type | Description |
| - | - |
| Deposit | Money collected from a customer has been deposited on your wallet. |
| Payout | Money has been paid out to a customer from your wallet. |
| Failed payout refund | Money initially reserved from your wallet for a payout has been returned due to the payout failing. |
| Refund | Money initially collected to your wallet has been refunded to the customer. |
| Failed refund reversal | Money initially reserved from your wallet for a refund has been returned due to the refund failing. |
| Remittance | Money has been sent from your wallet for a remittance. |
| Failed remittance refund | Money initially reserved from your wallet for a remittance has been returned due to the remittance failing. |
| Deposit pass through fees | A fee charged by the Mobile Money Operator (MMO) for a deposit. |
| Payout pass through fees | A fee charged by the Mobile Money Operator (MMO) for a payout. |
| Refund pass-through fees | A fee charged by the Mobile Money Operator (MMO) for a refund. |
| Remittance pass-through fees | A fee charged by the Mobile Money Operator (MMO) for a remittance. |
| Deposit PawaPay fees | A fee charged by PawaPay for a deposit. |
| Payout PawaPay fees | A fee charged by PawaPay for a payout. |
| PawaPay refund fee | A fee charged by PawaPay for a refund. |
| PawaPay remittance fee | A fee charged by PawaPay for a remittance. |
| Top up | Funds sent by you have been added to your wallet. Read more about [Topping up your wallets](/dashboard/topping_up). |
| Top up - Wallet to Wallet transfer | Funds have been moved into this wallet from another of your PawaPay wallets. |
| Withdrawal | Funds withdrawn from your wallet to be settled to your bank. |
| Withdrawal - Wallet to Wallet transfer | Funds have been moved from this wallet to another of your PawaPay wallets. |
| Cancelled withdrawal reversal | A withdrawal was cancelled and the funds have been returned to your wallet. |

### Adjustments and compensations

We record these manually to correct your balance. The Reason column explains each one.

| Transaction type | Description |
| - | - |
| Adjustment - Collections received | Adds successful deposits that were not credited to your wallet. |
| Adjustment - Collections not credited | Deducts deposits that were credited to your wallet in error. |
| Adjustment - Payouts not debited | Deducts successful payouts that were not debited from your wallet. |
| Adjustment - Payouts debited in error | Deducts an extra debit made for a payout, for example when the MMO debited it twice. |
| Adjustment - Payout reversal by MMO | Adds back a payout that the MMO reversed. |
| Adjustment - MNO interest disbursement | Adds interest paid out by the MMO. |
| Adjustment - Pass-through fees - Rebate | Adds a rebate on MMO pass-through fees. |
| Adjustment - Pass-through fee reimbursement | Adds back MMO pass-through fees. |
| Adjustment - Excise tax | Deducts excise tax. |
| Adjustment - Withholding tax | Deducts withholding tax. |
| Adjustment - Bank charges | Deducts bank charges. |
| Adjustment - Other (+) | Adds an amount for a reason not covered by another type. |
| Adjustment - Other | Deducts an amount for a reason not covered by another type. |
| Compensation - Payouts debited in error | Adds back payouts that were debited from your wallet in error. |
| Compensation - PawaPay fees reimbursement | Adds back PawaPay fees. |
| Compensation - Other | Adds compensation for a reason not covered by another type. |
| Manual pass-through fee deduction | Deducts MMO pass-through fees. |
| Manual PawaPay fee deduction | Deducts PawaPay fees. |


# Wallets
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/finances/wallets



On the PawaPay platform, all of your mobile money is stored in wallets. In most cases, wallets are issued per country and hold all your available mobile money in that country.

On the Wallets page, you can see the balances of all your wallets and view a breakdown of the transactions that have affected each wallet.

## Balance overview

In the balance overview section, you can see each of your wallets and their:

* Country
* Current balance
* Currency
* Active providers (MMOs)

Click on a wallet to instantly view its breakdown in the Wallet breakdown panel.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/wallets-balance-overview-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> In normal circumstances, wallets are issued per country.\
> If a wallet shows **No active provider**, none of your payment flows are currently active for it.

## Wallet breakdown

When you select a wallet, its breakdown is displayed automatically.

Choose a quick filter to quickly view yesterday, last week, or last month. Or select a custom date range using the date picker.

![](/images/dashboard/finances/wallet-breakdown-presets-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> The wallet breakdown is displayed from **midnight to midnight** in the UTC time zone. You can select a period of up to **one month** at a time.

The breakdown shows how your wallet balance has changed over the selected period.

Together with the opening and closing balance, you will see the total value of:

* Deposits
* Split Deposits
* Refunds
* Payouts
* Split Payouts
* Remittances
* Fees
* Withdrawals
* Top ups
* Adjustments
* Compensations
* Uncategorized

Money in is displayed as a positive value in green. Money out is displayed as a negative value in red, in brackets.

### Export wallet breakdown

You can export the breakdown as a CSV or PDF file at any time by selecting "Export statement".

![](/images/dashboard/finances/wallet-breakdown-export-light.svg)


# Global search
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/global_search



Any payment on our platform can be found quickly and easily using our global search which is always at the top left corner of the dashboard.

This functionality is available to users with the Transactions role.
Read more about [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles).

## How to search

Enter one of the following into the search bar:

* Phone number (MSISDN)
* MMO Transaction ID
* Transaction ID (deposit ID, payout ID, refund ID)
* Full Metadata value
  * Metadata is searched based on full value of the metadata field. For example, searching for 12345, to find INV-12345, will not find results.

![](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/HJiOScAQ34lKT2Kj/images/dashboard/global_search.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=HJiOScAQ34lKT2Kj\&q=85\&s=e3ef69f7813fe7b258721f2f997a3cb1)

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Please note!**
>
> Global search finds transactions from the last three months.


# PawaPay Dashboard
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/introduction



From the PawaPay Dashboard you can manage all your payments and operations in one single place. Learn more:

> **[Your wallet balances](/dashboard/finances/wallets)**
>
> See how much funds you have across all the different markets you operate in.

> **[Check your statements](/dashboard/finances/statements)**
>
> Make sure the funds you have are as they are supposed to be.

> **[Find any transaction](/dashboard/transactions/deposits)**
>
> To provide the best support to your customers, all payments in any market and with any MMO are available in one place along with their live status.

> **[Global search](/dashboard/global_search)**
>
> Global search finds any payment from the last three months quickly, regardless of where it was made.

> **[Manage access](/dashboard/user_management/inviting_users)**
>
> Manage users with sophisticated access controls and high level of security and auditability.

> **[Configuration](/dashboard/other/system_conf/api_tokens)**
>
> Get everything set up for your integration quickly and easily.


# Audit logs
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/other/audit_log



Key actions taken in our dashboard are tracked and visible in the Audit Log.
You can find here any changes to user permissions, new users invited, who signed into the portal and when, etc.

This functionality is available to users with the Administrator role. Read more about [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles).

> [!WARNING]
>
> We strongly recommend using only personalised accounts on our platform - all accounts should be accessible to a single person.
> This allows for compliant auditability of all actions taken on our dashboard.

## Searching and filtering

Please choose the time period you are interested in and press "Apply".

![](/images/dashboard/other/audit-search-log-light.svg)

The following information will be available for each action:

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| Time | The date and time when this action took place. |
| Action | The type of action that took place. Find below the glossary of all actions tracked. |
| Performed by | The user who took this action. |
| Description | Further details about the action. *For example, for the ROLE CHANGED action, it would include which role was assigned to the user.* |
| Affected user | The user who was affected by this action. *As an example, for whom the Role was changed.* |

You can always further filter down the results from the search bar or by pressing the filter icon in a column header.

![](/images/dashboard/other/audit-filter-log-light.svg)

As an example, you could search for the name of the user, which would filter the results to show all actions taken by or affecting this particular person during the selected time period.

## Glossary of actions

| Action | Description |
| - | - |
| User login | User has signed into the dashboard. |
| User invited | A new user has been invited into the dashboard. |
| User invite re-sent | A user has been resent the invitation email. |
| User registered | A user has activated their account in the dashboard. |
| User status change | User has been disabled or re-enabled to access the dashboard. |
| Password changed | A user has changed their password. |
| Role changed | A user's role has changed. Read more about [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles). |
| Country access changed | The countries that the user is able to see in the dashboard have changed. Read more about country-level access restrictions from [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles). |
| Mobile money API token generated | A new API token has been generated for your account. |
| Revoke API token | An API token has been revoked. |
| Batch disbursement | A new batch disbursement has been initiated. |
| Domain added | A new email domain has been added to the email domain whitelist. |
| Invite cancelled | A pending invitation has been deleted. |
| Enqueued payout cancellation | An enqueued payout has been cancelled. Read more about [cancelling enqueued payouts](/dashboard/transactions/cancel_enqueued). |
| Merchant admin invited | The first administrator of your account has been created at sign-up and sent a confirmation email. |
| Merchant admin confirmed | The first administrator of your account has confirmed their email address. |


# Batch disbursements
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/other/batch_disbursements



You can use our Batch disbursements page to initiate multiple disbursements at the same time directly from our dashboard.

This functionality is available to users with the Batch Disbursements role. Read more about [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles).

## Creating your batch disbursements file

You can download a template directly from the dashboard to create a new batch disbursement file.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-batch-template-light.svg)

The template contains the following columns to be filled out by you.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| Country | The country in which the recipient of the disbursement resides in. |
| Telco | The Mobile Money Operator (MMO) that the recipient's mobile money wallet is registered with. |
| Currency | The currency for this disbursement. |
| MSISDN | The phone number of the recipient of this disbursement. |
| Amount | The amount you wish to disburse. |
| Description | The description of this disbursement. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> The MSISDN must:
>
> * not start with a + sign
> * start with the country code
>
> The description must:
>
> * Be at least 4 characters
> * Not be longer than 22 characters
> * Contain only letters, numbers and spaces
> * Not contain any special characters

> [!TIP]
>
> You can find all the supported Country, Telco, and Currency combinations from [our API docs](/v2/docs/providers).

### Example batch disbursement file

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-batch-example-file-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> A maximum of 1000 disbursements can be added to a single batch disbursement file.

## Uploading your batch disbursement file

After filling in your file, you can proceed to upload it into our system for validation. Your file will be validated for formatting errors and to ensure your account has configuration in place to disburse to the specified MMOs.

The results of validation will be shown directly in the dashboard.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-batch-validation-light.svg)

| Result | Description |
| - | - |
| Ready | The transaction is ready to be disbursed. |
| Failed | Transaction is not valid. You can hover on the "Failed" result to see the failure reason. |

## Fixing validation failures

When encountering failures in your batch disbursement file, you can press the "Download Results" button to retrieve your batch disbursement file together with the failure reasons.

You can fix the errors in this file and attempt to upload again.

> [!TIP]
>
> You can re-upload the file downloaded by pressing the "Download Results" button to attempt again.
>
> You do not need to remove the failure reasons from this file before re-uploading.

## Initiating the batch disbursements

If every transaction is "Ready", you can press the "Schedule payment" button to initiate the disbursements.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-batch-schedule-light.svg)


# API tokens
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/other/system_conf/api_tokens



The PawaPay Merchant API can only be used with an authentication token. You can read more about how this token can be used to access our API from our [API docs](/using_the_api#authentication).

This functionality is available to users with the Technical Administration role. Read more about [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles).

## Generating an API token

Press the "Generate token" button to generate an API token. You can have at most 10 active API tokens at a time.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-generate-token-light.svg)

> [!TIP]
>
> You can use the "Copy to clipboard" button to easily copy the API token.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Store your token safely as PawaPay does not store your token after generating it for security reasons.**
>
> **You need to configure your [Callback URLs](/using_the_api#callback-urls) to be able to generate API tokens.**

## Active API tokens

Your active API tokens are listed together with the information about who generated them, when they were generated, and the Token ID.
Note that the Token ID is not usable as the token itself but is only used for identifying a specific token when contacting our support team.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-active-tokens-light.svg)

## Revoking tokens

If you need to revoke an API token, you can press the "Revoke" button which is found under the "Actions" column.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-revoke-token-light.svg)

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Revoking an API token will immediately stop all payments that use the given token to authenticate API calls!**

## Signed requests

You can enable PawaPay to only accept signed requests for financial calls. You will need to provide us with the public key of the key pair you are signing your requests with.

### Accepted algorithms

We accept 4 kinds of encryption algorithms:

* [RSASSA-PSS Using SHA-512](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9421#name-rsassa-pss-using-sha-512)
* [RSASSA-PKCS1-v1\_5 Using SHA-256](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9421#name-rsassa-pkcs1-v1_5-using-sha)
* [ECDSA Using Curve P-256 DSS and SHA-256](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9421#name-ecdsa-using-curve-p-256-dss)
* [ECDSA Using Curve P-384 DSS and SHA-384](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9421#name-ecdsa-using-curve-p-384-dss)

### Adding a public key

**1. Add your public key**

You can add your public key by navigating to the API Security tab and pressing on “Add public key”.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-add-public-key-light.svg)

**2. Enter public key details**

You will then be presented a window where you can:

1. Name your public key
2. Enter the public key itself
3. Choose whether you want to immediately start accepting only signed requests (shown when you add your first key)

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-enter-public-key-light.svg)

After successfully adding a key you will be able to view and remove it.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-view-key-light.svg)

You can also switch this feature on and off by using the toggle. Switching the feature off **will not** remove any existing keys.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-signed-only-light.svg)

## Signed callbacks

Enable this feature to make PawaPay sign all callbacks.
You can then verify those signatures when receiving the callback to ensure they have not been tampered with and are coming from PawaPay.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-signed-callbacks-light.svg)

Read more about signed callbacks in our [API docs](/using_the_api#signatures-in-callbacks).


# Callback URLs
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/other/system_conf/callback_urls



Our platform uses callbacks to notify you of the final statuses of payments. You can read more about how callbacks are used on our platform from [our API docs](/using_the_api#callback-urls).

This functionality is available to users with the Technical Administration role. Read more about [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles).

## Specifying the callback URLs

Please enter the URL at which you wish to receive notifications about the [final statuses](/dashboard/transactions/transaction_statuses) of payments. You can use the same URL for all types.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-callback-urls-light.svg)

> [!WARNING]
>
> Ensure you enter the correct URL.
> If you are using a firewall, ensure that you have whitelisted our IPs.
> The IPs can be found in our [API docs](/using_the_api#callback-urls).

If you do not plan to use our API (e.g., you are only planning to use only our [Batch disbursements](/dashboard/other/batch_disbursements) or will be polling for final status, please indicate that by checking the below checkbox.

![](/images/dashboard/other/dev-callbacks-opt-out-light.svg)


# How to log in
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/signing_in



The PawaPay Dashboard supports two methods of user authentication: traditional password-based authentication and Google-based authentication.

If you opt for Google-based authentication, your organization must already utilize [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com/), or a comparable service where Google manages email addresses. This feature facilitates a seamless login process, allowing users to access the Dashboard using their existing Google accounts.

> [!TIP]
>
> We recommend forcing 2-step verification on your Google Workspace account for increased security.

## Logging into the dashboard

#### Authentication with username and password

Go to our [log in page](https://dashboard.pawapay.io/), enter your email address, and press "Continue with email".

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/login-enter-email-light.svg)

Enter your password and press "Continue with email".

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/login-enter-password-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Our dashboard follows [OWASP ASVS Level 3](https://owasp.org/www-pdf-archive/OWASPApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard3.0.pdf) password policy.

If [two-factor authentication](/dashboard/user_management/security) is enabled for your company, you'll be prompted for a verification code (OTP) sent to your email, unless you've selected the "Remember me" checkbox, which remembers your device for 30 days (up to 3 devices). Enter the code and press "Continue" to be redirected to the PawaPay Dashboard.

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/login-verification-code-light.svg)

#### Authentication with Google

Go to our [log in page](https://dashboard.pawapay.io/) and select "Continue with Google". There's no need to enter your email here.

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/login-continue-google-light.svg)

If you've chosen Google as your authentication method, the Dashboard will present you an option to authenticate via signing in with your Google account.

![Choose Google account](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/Ia3epkqdnk0_YmHS/images/dashboard/signing_in/choose_google_account.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=Ia3epkqdnk0_YmHS\&q=85\&s=c975f50a5b39854f38bd2ebc79cc6e0d)

> [!NOTE]
>
> When using multiple Google accounts (i.e., business and personal), make sure you choose the account that was used to invite you to our Dashboard.

### Resetting your password

Enter your email on our [log in page](https://dashboard.pawapay.io/) and press "Continue with email". Then select "Forgot your password?".

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/login-forgot-password-link-light.svg)

Enter your email and press "Reset my password".

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/login-forgot-password-light.svg)

You will receive an email with a link to reset your password. Press on the "Reset password" button.

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/email-password-reset-light.svg)

You will be forwarded to the password reset page where you can enter your new password. When done, press on "Change my password".

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/login-change-password-light.svg)

You will then see a confirmation. Press "Login to the dashboard" to go to our [log in page](https://dashboard.pawapay.io/) and log in with your new password.

## Activating your account

When invited to our dashboard, you will receive an invitation email with an activation link. Activate your account within 30 days.

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/email-account-activation-light.svg)

Pressing "Activate your account" will take you to the account activation page where you are asked to read and accept our Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy, and choose your authentication method - Google or username and password - if both are available to you.

> [!TIP]
>
> The password meter at the bottom of the "Password" input helps you choose a strong password to secure your account.

![](/images/dashboard/signing_in/activate-account-password-meter-light.svg)

Pressing "Activate" will take you to our Dashboard [log in page](https://dashboard.pawapay.io/).


# Platform and MMO status
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/status



Any relevant information about incidents and maintenance that affect your merchant account will be displayed on the top right corner of the PawaPay Dashboard.

![](/images/dashboard/incidents-button-light.svg)

Pressing the button will expand your view and provide more details on the ongoing incidents and upcoming maintenance.

![](/images/dashboard/incidents-expanded-light.svg)

Pressing "Read more" will direct you to the incident page with more information about it.

The "Status Page" button will direct you to our [status page](https://status.pawapay.io/).

> [!TIP]
>
> On the [status page](https://status.pawapay.io/) you can subscribe to receive updates about incidents through different channels like e-mail, Slack and more.

## Availability statuses of MMOs

| Status | Description |
| - | - |
| Operational | Service is operating as expected. |
| Degraded performance | Degraded performance for some transactions. |
| Partial outage | Degraded performance with intermittent unavailability. |
| Major outage | Service is unavailable and no transactions are accepted for processing. |
| Under maintenance | There is an active maintenance window. Degraded performance or intermittent unavailability might occur. |

> [!TIP]
>
> Our support and payment operation teams work 24/7 and are aware of, and acting on, any statuses shown on our status page.
> We provide regular updates on the progress of resolving all issues that arise.

## More about MMO availability

To provide the best experience for your customers, we suggest implementing our Correspondent Availability Status endpoints.
This allows you to inform your customers proactively about MMO downtime.

Read more from our [API docs](/v1/api-reference/toolkit/availability).


# Contacting our support
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/support



> [!TIP]
>
> Our dedicated support team operates around the clock, 24/7, to assist you with any queries you may have regarding your transactions or the functionalities of our platform.

You can contact our Support team by signing into the PawaPay Dashboard and selecting the "Payment Support" link from the "Help" menu in the top-right of the Dashboard.

![](/images/dashboard/help-menu-payment-support-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Note: "Payment Support" is only available on Production, not the Sandbox.

Then select the type of query you have.

![](https://mintcdn.com/pawapay/KeSN8kn4aGt-0baQ/images/dashboard/support_widget.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=KeSN8kn4aGt-0baQ\&q=85\&s=3e1e0852f984fcd1fd734d4aee289d7a)

#### Payments

From the *Payments* form, select an option from the *Category* dropdown — these include:

| Category | Description |
| - | - |
| Missing deposit enquiry | To enquire about deposits which do not reflect in the PawaPay system, but are deemed as successful by the MMO.  *For example, you have a MMO financial ID of a successful deposit transaction that you are unable to locate in the PawaPay Dashboard.* |
| Deposit status enquiry | To enquire about deposits which reflect in the PawaPay system, but you are seeking for further clarification. |
| Payout status enquiry | To enquire about payouts which reflect in the PawaPay system, but you are seeking for further clarification. |
| Other | In case you have any other questions about transactions on your PawaPay wallets. |

##### What to include in a *Payments* request?

To help us resolve your request quickly and effectively, please include as many relevant details as possible. This will allow us to identify, investigate, and address the issue more efficiently.

| Detail | Description |
| - | - |
| Amount | The amount in country specific currency. |
| MMO transaction ID | This is the ID that the customer would see for this transaction. *Particularly important for reconciling payments that do not appear in our dashboard or are not in a final state. Read more about [Transaction statuses](/dashboard/transactions/transaction_statuses) .* |
| Phone number (MSISDN) | The phone number of the customer.  *For mobile money, this is the equivalent of a bank account or card number.* |
| Date and time | The date and time the problem occurred.  *Particularly important for reconciling payments that do not appear in our dashboard.* |
| Transaction ID | The ID of the deposit, payout or refund as seen in our dashboard. |
| Additional details & attachments | Any additional details about your request, plus any relevant attachments (optional). |

#### Other enquiries

From here you can enquire about:

| Category | Description |
| - | - |
| Financial statement enquiry | Use this if you have any questions about the data displayed on your financial statements. |
| General Finance & Treasury enquiry | In case you have any other questions related to Treasury or Finance. |
| Raise a complaint | Please use this form to submit a formal complaint regarding our service, product or an issue at hand that requires further investigation. We take all feedback seriously and aim to resolve issues promptly. |
| Other | In case you have any other general questions. |


# Topping up your wallets
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/topping_up

How to pre-fund your PawaPay wallet so you can make payouts.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To avoid any delays, please make sure that all funds for payouts/disbursements are sent from an account owned by your company. If you need to send funds through a contractual partner, please go through the [adding a Liquidity Partner](#adding-a-liquidity-partner) journey described below on this page.

In order to make payouts via our API, your wallet must have sufficient funds available. Where a payout request is made and the wallet has insufficient balance to complete the transaction, the transaction will fail.

Accordingly, if you intend to use payouts you will be required to pre-fund (top up) your PawaPay wallet.

In order to streamline the process you are encouraged to follow the instructions below whenever a top up is being made to your PawaPay wallet.

## Send your funds to the correct bank account

When sending funds to top up your wallet in a particular country, you are requested to send those funds to the bank account for the respective market which will be presented to you in the PawaPay Dashboard. Remember to always include your account specific ID to each payment you make. This will also be presented to you in the payment instruction we give.

> [!WARNING]
>
> To use Top ups in the Dashboard your merchant account must have either payouts or remittances enabled.
> You must also have either the "Top ups" role, or be an "Administrator".
>
> If you don’t have access, please contact your account administrator or the PawaPay team.

## Creating a top up

You can start a new top up at any time from the **Top ups** page in the Dashboard. Click **Create new top up** and the Dashboard will walk you through five short steps. If your account has both payouts and remittances enabled, an extra step asks what the funds are for. A top up from another PawaPay wallet skips the currency and payment steps.

[Arcade demo](https://app.arcade.software/share/2u0a6uaUzA0KR80T21ZH)

**1. Choose the wallets you want to fund**

Select one or more wallets that will receive the money. Each wallet is shown with its country and currency — for example, *Uganda UGX* or *Ghana GHS*. You can tick as many as you need, or use **Select all** to pick them all at once.

If you don't see a wallet you expect to be there, your PawaPay account may not be set up for that market yet.

**2. Choose how you want to fund your balance**

Pick the method you will use to send us the money. See [Choosing a funding method](#choosing-a-funding-method) below for a plain-English explanation of each option.

**3. Choose a currency**

Pick the currency you will send. The Dashboard only shows currencies that are valid for the wallets and funding method you chose in the previous steps. If something isn't listed, it isn't currently supported for your selection.

**4. Enter the amounts**

For each wallet you picked in step 1, type in how much you want credited. The Dashboard keeps a running **Total amount to top up** on the right so you can see the full amount you need to transfer.

**5. Send us the money and upload your Proof of Payment**

This is the final step. The Dashboard will show you:

* The **bank account** you should send the funds to.
* Your **unique merchant code** — a short reference you must include with the transfer (see [Your unique merchant code](#your-unique-merchant-code) below).
* An **expected timeline**. We always try to process top ups as soon as possible but the timelines vary country by country.

Once you've made the transfer from your bank, come back to this screen and upload your Proof of Payment — a screenshot or PDF of the SWIFT confirmation or bank receipt. Then hit **Top up**.

## Choosing a funding method

Step 2 of the wizard asks how you want to fund your balance. You will see one or more of the following options — the ones available depend on your account setup:

> **Your bank account**
>
> Send funds from a bank account owned by your company via a standard bank/SWIFT transfer. This is the most common option. The Dashboard will show you the PawaPay bank account you should send the money to at step 5.

> **PawaPay Wallet (wallet to wallet)**
>
> Move money you already hold in one PawaPay wallet into another PawaPay wallet. You'll be asked to pick which PawaPay wallet the money should come from.

> **Liquidity Partner**
>
> A Liquidity Partner is a third party — for example, an aggregator or on-the-ground partner — that funds your wallet on your behalf. Before you can use one, they need to be approved by our Treasury team. See [Adding a Liquidity Partner](#adding-a-liquidity-partner) below.

## Your unique merchant code

Every top up comes with a **unique merchant code**, which is a short reference shown on the payment instructions screen.

> [!WARNING]
>
> You **must** include this code in the reference / description / narration field of your bank transfer. Without it, our Treasury team cannot match your payment to your account, which will delay your top up.

![](/images/dashboard/top_ups/topup-payment-reference-light.svg)

The Dashboard has a **Copy** button next to the code so you can paste it straight into your bank's transfer form. The same code needs to be reused across your top ups as it identifies your account, not the individual payment. Some bank accounts need their own reference instead. In that case the Dashboard shows that reference, so always use the code shown.

## Adding a Liquidity Partner

If someone other than your own company is going to send us the funds — for example, a local aggregator or a contractual partner — then they need to be onboarded as a **Liquidity Partner** first. This is a one-time setup per partner.

![](/images/dashboard/top_ups/topup-add-liquidity-partner-light.svg)

### How to add one

**1. Open the Liquidity Partners page**

From the **Top ups** page, click **Add liquidity partner**, then **Add liquidity partner** again on the **Liquidity Partners** page (or use the **Add new Liquidity Partner** link inside step 2 of the top up wizard).

**2. Fill in the partner's details**

You'll be asked for:

* **Liquidity Partner name** — the legal name of the partner.
* **Your relationship with the partner** — a short description of how you work together.
* **Line of business** — what the partner does.
* **Country coverage** — the countries they're licensed / allowed to operate in.

**3. Upload the supporting documents**

Attach:

* **Licenses** — relevant financial or operating licenses the partner holds.
* **KYC documents** — incorporation documents, plus identification for shareholders with 5% or more stake and for directors.

You can upload multiple files in PDF, JPEG or PNG format, up to 5 MB each.

**4. Submit for review**

Click **Submit**. Your request goes to our Treasury team for review. You can track it on the **Liquidity Partners** page — the status will show as **In review** until it's been approved or rejected. You may be contacted by our team via email for further clarification.

Once a Liquidity Partner is **Approved**, they will appear as a selectable option under *Liquidity Partner* on step 2 of the top up wizard.

## After you submit a top up

Once you've uploaded your Proof of Payment, your top up lands on the **Top ups** page with a status you can track:

| Status | What it means |
| :- | :- |
| **Pending** | We've received your submission but haven't started processing it yet. |
| **In progress** | Our Treasury team is reviewing the payment and crediting your wallet. |
| **Completed** | The funds are in your wallet and ready to use for payouts. |
| **Failed** | Something went wrong with processing — our team will be in touch. |
| **Rejected** | The Proof of Payment couldn't be matched to a payment we've received. |
| **Cancelled** | You (or our team) cancelled the top up before it was processed. |

You can open any top up to see its details per wallet, add a comment for our Treasury team, or download the Proof of Payment you uploaded. While a top up is **Pending**, you can also cancel it.

> [!TIP]
>
> Need to do another top up that looks just like a past one? Use **Repeat top up** on any completed top up. The Dashboard will pre-fill the wizard with the same wallets, funding method and currency so you can adjust the amounts and submit.


# Callback resend
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/transactions/callback_resend



When a payment is completed, we communicate the final status to your systems by sending a callback.
However, delivery of these callbacks may be unsuccessful due to network instabilities, downtime in the receiving system, or similar issues.
In such scenarios, you have the option to resend the callback through our dashboard.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Callbacks can only be resent for payments initiated within the last 90 days.
> Older payments remain visible in the dashboard and their status can still be checked — only the callback resend is no longer available for them.

The option to resend a callback is only available when our initial attempt to deliver it has been unsuccessful. In the event of a problematic transaction, you can navigate to the respective payment details page. Here, you'll find the option to resend the callback.

![](/images/dashboard/transactions/tx-callback-resend-light.svg)

To resend the callback, click on the 'Resend callback' button.

The process should conclude within a few seconds, and a confirmation message will appear upon its successful completion.

> [!TIP]
>
> There is also an option to initiate this process via an API call.
> Read more about this from our API documentation for [deposits](/v1/api-reference/deposits/resend-deposit-callback), [payouts](/v1/api-reference/payouts/resend-payout-callback) and [refunds](/v1/api-reference/refunds/resend-refund-callback).


# Cancel enqueued payout
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/transactions/cancel_enqueued



During certain incidents involving Mobile Money Operators (MMOs), PawaPay may temporarily suspend the processing of payouts.
We understand the importance of maintaining transaction flow.
Therefore, we continue to accept your payout requests during these periods.

These requests are assigned a status of **Enqueued**.
This status indicates that your payout request has been received and is in line for processing as soon as the network stabilizes.
However, you have the option to cancel these transactions by navigating to the respective payment details page and initiating a cancellation from there.

![](/images/dashboard/transactions/tx-cancel-enqueued-light.svg)

To cancel an Enqueued transaction, click on the "Cancel transaction" button.

The process should conclude within a few seconds, and a confirmation message will appear upon its successful completion.

> [!TIP]
>
> There is also an option to initiate this process via an API call.
> Read more regarding this functionality from our [API documentation](/v1/api-reference/payouts/cancel-enqueued-payout).


# Deposit details
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/transactions/deposit_details



You can see the details of a deposit by using either our [Global search](/dashboard/global_search) or [Deposits](/dashboard/transactions/deposits) search functionality and clicking on the specific payment.

You can find the glossary of the data found on the deposit details from the [Deposits](/dashboard/transactions/deposits) documentation.

All possible statuses of transactions are documented in [Transaction statuses](/dashboard/transactions/transaction_statuses).

## Successful deposit

![](/images/dashboard/transactions/tx-deposit-completed-light.svg)

> [!TIP]
>
> On successful deposits, the Provider Transaction ID is available. This ID is also available to the customer on their SMS receipt or their transaction history. When contacted by a customer, their transaction can be found using this ID.

## Failed deposit

![](/images/dashboard/transactions/tx-deposit-failed-light.svg)

> [!NOTE]
>
> We constantly monitor and improve the failure reasons to be as precise and accurate as possible.\
> Some Mobile Money Operators (MMO) do not provide specific failure reasons for failed transactions.


# Deposits
Source: https://docs.pawapay.io/dashboard/transactions/deposits



You can find all deposits made on our platform on the Deposits page.

![](/images/dashboard/transactions/tx-deposits-search-light.svg)

This functionality is available to users with the Transactions role. Read more about [User roles](/dashboard/user_management/user_roles).

## Search for deposits

Please choose the time period you are interested in by clicking on the time period selector. You can also use the quick links next to the selector to quickly see transactions made in the last hour, today, yesterday, or the current week.

If you are interested in transactions of a specific Mobile Money Operator (MMO), you can filter by picking them from the Providers dropdown.

Pressing "Apply filters" will show you the results.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A maximum of 10,000 records will be shown. If your search results in more than that, the oldest 10,000 will be visible in your results.

## Glossary of results

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| Creation date | The date and time at which this deposit was initiated. Time is in the UTC time zone. |
| Phone number | The phone number of the party being collected from. |
| Provider Transaction ID | The ID for this transaction specified by the MMO.  **Please note!** This ID is visible to your customers in their SMS receipts or Mobile Money applications transaction history. |
| Amount | The amount on the original deposit request. |
| Currency | The currency in which this transaction took place. |
| Flow subtype | The type of deposit. |
| Status | The current status of this transaction. Read more about statuses from [Transaction statuses](/dashboard/transactions/transaction_statuses). |
| Country | The country in which this transaction took place. |
| Provider | The Mobile Money Operator who carried out the transaction. |
| Reason | The reason for this payment specified by you as the `statementDescription` in our API. Read more about our deposits in our API from our [API docs](/v1/api-reference/deposits/request-deposit). |
